name: Coron
tagline: Sunken Japanese warships, crystal freshwater lakes, hot springs and limestone islands, in the Calamian archipelago north of Palawan.
highlight: Swimming in the warm, glass-clear waters of Kayangan Lake, ringed by steep limestone cliffs.
shortDescription: A base for the Calamian Islands, with world-class wreck diving, Kayangan and Barracuda Lakes, Twin Lagoon, Siete Pecados reef snorkelling and Maquinit hot springs.
metaDescription: A Coron travel guide: Kayangan Lake, Twin Lagoon, WWII wreck diving, Barracuda Lake, Maquinit hot springs, Mount Tapyas, island hopping tours, where to stay and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Francisco B. Reyes Airport, Busuanga (USU), about 45 minutes

image.alt: The clear turquoise water of Kayangan Lake in Coron

intro: Coron is a town on Busuanga Island in the Calamian Islands, north of Palawan, and the base for a spectacular area of steep limestone islands, lakes and reefs. In September 1944, a US Navy air attack sank a fleet of Japanese supply ships in Coron Bay, and about a dozen wrecks now lie at depths of 10 to 40 metres, making it one of the best wreck-diving destinations in the world.

Above water, the highlights are Kayangan Lake, often called the cleanest lake in Asia, a brackish lake in a crater ringed by cliffs, and Barracuda Lake, where a thermocline makes the water suddenly warm. Twin Lagoon is two lagoons separated by a rock, and you swim through a gap from one to the other. There are also snorkelling reefs, beaches, and the Maquinit hot springs, a saltwater pool heated by geothermal activity.

The town has a busy waterfront and a viewpoint at Mount Tapyas reached by 700 steps. Most visitors spend three days on island tours, dives and relaxation, and many combine Coron with El Nido by ferry. Note that much of the area belongs to the Tagbanua people, who manage several sites, and fees support their ancestral domain.
